subject: Blueshore discovery: latency/throughput SLOs & deployment milestones
messages:
From: Jasmine Liu <jasmine.l@redwoodinference.com>
To: Samir Khan <samir.k@blueshorehealth.com>, Priya Desai <priya.desai@blueshorehealth.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica.p@redwoodinference.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.k@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Thu, 21 Oct 2027 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: Blueshore discovery: latency/throughput SLOs & deployment milestones

Hi Samir / Priya —

Thanks for the time today. Quick recap from our call and next steps so we keep momentum:

Summary of pain and goals (what you told us):
- Primary product: patient triage chatbot integrated into your appointment flow. Peak traffic around 08:00–10:00 ET.
- Current pain: unpredictable token costs and two incidents last month where latency spikes caused timeouts in the frontend.
- Target SLOs: 99th percentile latency target ≈ 150 ms for short chat queries (<= 256 tokens); 95th percentile throughput target ~300 req/s sustained during peak windows.
- Security: HIPAA + VPC isolation required; SOC 2 report and audit logs needed for procurement.
- Model requirements: open-family model acceptable, prefer 70B-class (quantized) for accuracy on clinical prompts, possibility to fall back to smaller model for non-critical paths.

Key technical constraints we discussed:
- GCP us-central1 primary region; on-prem data store for PHI that must not leave VPC.
- Expect mixed small/medium/long sequences — heavy KV cache benefits for repeat prefixes (saves ~35% token cost).
- Will need canary deploys and an automatic fallback policy for capacity exhaustion.

Immediate next steps (owners & timing):
1) SLO matrix + proposed topology (Redwood) — I attached a starter SLO matrix (blueshore-slo-matrix.xlsx) and a topology sketch (proposed-topology-diagram.png). Action: Redwood to update with sizing after traffic sample. ETA: Tue 10/26 (Vivek leading).
2) Traffic sample (Blueshore) — Samir, please share 48–72h anonymized sampling of request sizes & arrival patterns. File name suggestion: current-traffic-sample.csv.
3) Security questionnaire / SOC2 request (Blueshore) — Procurement: we'll send SOC2 + SOC2 auditor contact.
4) Deep technical session with infra & security (all parties) — propose Wed 10/27 or Thu 10/28. Vivek to run the ops/topology discussion; Monica to cover support/SLAs.
5) Cost ballpark for Dedicated vs Private (Redwood) — Redwood to provide a high-level cost delta for the two deployment modes once we have traffic sample.

Questions I left open for Redwood follow-up:
- Preferred quantization/profile for 70B on your workload (Vivek will recommend two safe profiles).
- Autoscaling headroom & burst capacity policy for the 300 req/s figure.

Attachments: blueshore-slo-matrix.xlsx, proposed-topology-diagram.png (starter drafts).

If that lines up, I’ll schedule the deep technical session for Wed 10/27 10:00–11:00 PT (01:00–02:00 ET) — let me know if that time is bad and Samir / Priya propose two alternate windows.

Thanks — pleasant to meet you both today.

Best,
Jasmine Liu
Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference
jasmine.l@redwoodinference.com

From: Samir Khan <samir.k@blueshorehealth.com>

Date: Thu, 21 Oct 2027 18:04:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Blueshore discovery: latency/throughput SLOs & deployment milestones

Jasmine — thanks for the thorough recap. High level: this matches our read. A couple of quick clarifications from engineering and procurement: 

1) Technical contacts: Priya Desai (included) is our infra lead (GCP + on-prem networking). For security & procurement, looping in procurement@blueshorehealth.com for SOC2 routing.
2) Traffic sample: attaching a 72h sample (current-traffic-sample.csv) — anonymized; includes arrival timestamps, token counts, and endpoint path.
3) Auto-fallback behavior: would prefer an agreement where the system can route lower-cost model variants first and transparently degrade quality for non-critical paths. Can Redwood provide a sketch of how routing + canary + fallback would work (high-level)?

We’re available for the deep tech session on Wed 10/27 13:00–14:00 ET (10:00–11:00 PT) — that works for me. Priya, can you confirm?

I’ve attached a short SOC2 checklist our procurement team expects (soc2-questionnaire.pdf) — procurement@blueshorehealth.com will follow up on contractual items and preferred procurement timeline (target: finalize vendor selection by Nov 15).

—Samir
Samir Khan
VP Product & Engineering
Blueshore Health
samir.k@blueshorehealth.com
From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.k@redwoodinference.com>
To: Jasmine Liu <jasmine.l@redwoodinference.com>, Monica Patel <monica.p@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Samir Khan <samir.k@blueshorehealth.com>, Priya Desai <priya.desai@blueshorehealth.com>
Date: Fri, 22 Oct 2027 01:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Blueshore discovery: latency/throughput SLOs & deployment milestones

Jasmine / Monica / Samir / Priya —

Thanks for the traffic sample, Samir — useful distribution. Quick ops notes after a first pass: 

Summary of findings (based on sample):
- 48–72h sample shows median request token length ~95, 90th ~320 tokens, occasional bursts (5–10 m windows) that push 350–420 req/s to the edge.
- Repeated prefixes for triage flows are common (~28% repeat), which means prefix/KV cache will give a meaningful reduction in GPU work and cost.

Topology options (attached: topology-options-v2.pdf):
Option A — Dedicated Hybrid (recommended initial):
- Redwood Dedicated pool (us-central1) + VPC peering to Blueshore on-prem for PHI.
- Autoscaler: target 300 req/s sustained, with burst capacity to 450 req/s for up to 10 minutes.
- KV cache warmers on edge nodes; prefix cache shared across the Dedicated pool.
- Canary plan: route 5% traffic for 48h to new model variant before ramping.
- Quantization profile: int4/awq-safe profile for 70B -> good accuracy with 2–3× perf improvement.

Option B — Private (customer-hosted control plane):
- On-prem inference appliances (for PHI processing) + Redwood control plane in a dedicated VPC.
- Better regulatory isolation but higher up-front ops and cost; suggested for when procurement insists on no PHI egress.

Immediate asks for accurate sizing/cost:
- Confirm desired production 99p latency target (we assumed 150 ms). If you can stretch to 200 ms for some non-critical endpoints we can reduce CPU/GPU footprint materially.
- Any retention requirement for KV cache (how long to keep entries)? Our default is 30 minutes for triage flows.

Prep for deep tech session Wed 10/27 13:00 ET:
- I’ll present the topology options + autoscale thresholds + quantization tradeoffs (20–25m). Monica will cover support/SLA + rollback windows. Jasmine to present procurement ask and timelines.

Attachments: topology-options-v2.pdf (sketch + cost delta table).

Action items I’ll own before the call: update the attached SLO matrix with measured p50/p95/p99 from the traffic sample and produce a short cost delta for Dedicated vs Private (ETA: Mon 10/25 COB).

-Vivek
Vivek Kulkarni
Solutions Engineering
Redwood Inference
vivek.k@redwoodinference.com

Subject: Re: Blueshore discovery: latency/throughput SLOs & deployment milestones

All — thanks. Wed 10/27 13:00 ET confirmed. Priya confirms she’ll join and bring the networking/security engineer as well. Procurement will sit in for the first 15 minutes only (contract timeline discussion).

Couple of quick checklist items we expect Redwood to bring to the meeting:
- Updated SLO matrix with p50/p95/p99 populated from the traffic sample; highlight where the 150 ms 99p comes from.
- Short slide on fallback and model-variant routing with a simple flow diagram (how requests are routed when pool capacity is low).
- Preliminary cost delta (Dedicated vs Private) at the high level — not a signed quote.

We look forward to the call — attaching our procurement SOC2 checklist (soc2-questionnaire.pdf) for reference.

See you both on Wed.

—Samir
